newsitem.title: UK: Several injured as gales batter Britain.
newsitem.headline: Several injured as gales batter Britain.

text.p: Fierce gales and heavy rain lashed Britain overnight, injuring several people, blocking roads and leaving thousands of homes without power, emergency services said on Tuesday.
No independent confirmation was available of a report by Britain's Press Association news agency that four people had been killed as the gales wreaked havoc with gusts of up to 145 kph (90 mph).
The agency also reported that two people were believed to be missing after being swept off a harbour wall by huge waves at Minehead in southwest England.
"As far as we are aware two people are thought to be missing and we will be continuing our inquiries today," it quoted a police spokesman as saying.
British meteorologists said the storms were a spin-off from Hurricane Lili, which caused widespread damage in Cuba and the Bahamas just over a week ago.
"While it lasted, it was a wild night," said a spokesman for the London Weather Centre.
Emergency services said several people had been injured in road accidents and by falling trees and roof tiles. They said it was too early to give exact figures.
Police and motoring organisations urged people not to travel unless it was absolutely necessary.

An Automobile Association spokesman said: "There were a lot of trees brought down, especially on rural roads... On this occasion everyone appears to have heeded the warnings we put out and stayed at home."

Rail services were badly disrupted in several areas and some cross-Channel ferries with hundreds of passengers on board were prevented from berthing at Dover, although the southeastern port remained open.
Thousands of people in southern England and Wales were left in darkness after power cables were torn down.
In Pembrokeshire in west Wales, fire fighters were called in to pump out flooded properties and to make damaged roofs safe.
An unmanned exploratory oil platform was ripped from its moorings in Portland harbour on England's south coast and hit rocks. A tug was sent to secure it.
Several major road bridges were closed to traffic for fear of vehicles being blown into the water. A smaller bridge over the river Wey, south of London, collapsed.
In the southern English town of Warminster, drivers were confused after the gales blew traffic lights round the wrong way.
